Profile.name: Jayanta Biswas
Profile.title: PhD Student in Geography & Graduate Research Assistant
Profile.short_bio: Spatial Geographer and GeoAI researcher specializing in knowledge-guided deep learning, fine-scale human mobility downscaling, satellite remote sensing, and spatial epidemiology.
Profile.about: I am a PhD student in Geography at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte (UNC Charlotte), working in the GeoHealth Dynamics Research (GeoHDR) Lab and Center for Applied Geographic Information Science (CAGIS) under the advisement of Dr. Yao Li. My research bridges GeoAI, deep learning ensembles, remote sensing, and spatial epidemiology to tackle global health challenges—such as precision malaria transmission modeling in sub-Saharan Africa. Prior to UNC Charlotte, I earned an M.Sc. in Earth Sciences from the University of Memphis, focusing on spatial econometrics and induced travel demand with TDOT/FHWA, and urban planning degrees from Khulna University, Bangladesh.

research_experience.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
research_experience.project_title: Deep learning-enhanced geospatial modeling for highlighting active disease transmission hotspots through accurate Human-Vector Contact Zones (HVCZ) prediction
highlights: Built a mass-conserving U-Net deep ensemble in PyTorch to downscale Meta human mobility data from ~5.5 km to 100 m grid across Zambia.
Engineered 38 environmental covariate layers at 100 m in Google Earth Engine (building footprints, road networks, nighttime lights, terrain, bioclimatic layers).
Incorporated annual WorldPop rasters to convert Meta activity counts into population-weighted mobility arrays.
Executed spatial block cross-validation across distinct agro-ecological and urban/rural zones to test spatial transferability.
Decomposed pixel-level uncertainties into epistemic and aleatoric variance, validating against Voronoi catchments from mobile Call Detail Records (CDR).

research_experience.project_title: Applying Induced Travel Study in Urban Areas in Tennessee
highlights: Estimated causal effects of lane-mile capacity expansions on VMT and AADT using facility-level OLS and 2SLS instrumental variable regression.
Overcame area-wide aggregation bias present in state-level induced travel studies.
Developed spatial econometric regression models tying historical satellite-derived land development (1985–2023) to highway improvements, published in Land (2025).

Publications.title: Improved remote sensing ecological index for monitoring urban sustainability: 100 resilient cities vs. non-resilient cities in South Asia
Publications.abstract: This study develops an improved Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) to evaluate urban ecological environment quality across four South Asian cities, comparing designated 100 Resilient Cities (Pune and Surat) with non-100RC counterparts (Chattogram and Nagpur) to examine how resilience frameworks impact environmental sustainability over decadal timescales.

Publications.title: Applying Induced Travel Study in Urban Areas in Tennessee
Publications.journal: Tennessee Department of Transportation & Federal Highway Administration (USDOT National Transportation Library)
Publications.corporate_creator: Center for Applied Earth Science and Engineering Research (CAESER), The University of Memphis
Publications.abstract: Investigates the causal impacts of highway capacity additions (road widening, new lane construction) on travel behavior and induced vehicle miles traveled (VMT) across urban corridors in Tennessee. By developing disaggregated facility-level instrumental variables, this study overcomes the area-wide aggregation bias of prior state-level research, providing empirical elasticity estimates to inform TDOT project screening, capital allocation, and sustainable regional planning.

Publications.title: Mapping wildfire dynamics: GeoAI-driven comparative analysis of deep and machine learning ensembles for susceptibility prediction in California
Publications.abstract: Investigates wildfire susceptibility across California through a rigorous comparative benchmarking of machine learning ensembles and deep neural networks. Evaluates both quantitative predictive accuracy and the spatial realism of hazard surfaces under computational constraints.

Publications.title: Land development 1985–2023 as a function of road improvement, employment, and mobility: A case study of Tennessee
Publications.abstract: Quantifies the spatial relationships between highway capacity additions, regional employment density, and urban land transformation across Tennessee from 1985 to 2023. Spatial regression models demonstrate that employment access acts as a widespread catalyst for urban expansion, whereas mobility (VMT) exhibits concentrated effects along higher-speed arterials.

Publications.title: Urban environmental degradation in Bangladesh: Insights from a weighted entropy ecological index
Publications.abstract: Introduces an objective entropy-weighted formulation of the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) to mitigate the subjectivity of PCA-based weighting and better account for moisture and water regimes across 12 major cities in Bangladesh, providing evidence for targeted urban environmental mitigation.

Publications.title: Tourism and environmental change in Saint Martin Island, Bangladesh: Insights from remote sensing data
Publications.journal: Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment
Publications.abstract: Utilizes high-resolution Sentinel-2 multispectral time series (2018–2024) to evaluate the environmental footprint of uncontrolled tourism development on Bangladesh's sole coral reef island, reaching classification accuracies of 94.6%–98.9% and documenting critical loss of vegetation and beach habitat.

Publications.title: Mapping and monitoring land use land cover dynamics employing Google Earth Engine and machine learning algorithms on Chattogram, Bangladesh
Publications.abstract: Leverages cloud computing on Google Earth Engine to train and evaluate supervised machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, Classification and Regression Trees) across multitemporal Landsat data, charting over two decades of rapid urbanization and vegetative fragmentation in Chattogram.

Publications.title: Spatiotemporal change detection of land use land cover (LULC) in Fashiakhali Wildlife Sanctuary (FKWS) impact area, Bangladesh employing remote sensing
Publications.abstract: Employs satellite image processing and GIS-based change detection to analyze habitat encroachment, agricultural conversion, and forest fragmentation in the peripheral buffer zone of Fashiakhali Wildlife Sanctuary over a 30-year period.

Publications.title: Land-use change and forest cover depletion in Bhawal National Park, Gazipur, Bangladesh from 2005 to 2020
Publications.abstract: Quantifies the depletion of over 2,284 hectares (~49%) of canopy cover in Bhawal National Park between 2005 and 2020 using Landsat-derived NDVI and land-use transition matrices, identifying industrialization and illegal settlement expansion as core drivers.

Presentations.title: A deep learning framework for fusing multi-modal environmental data to downscale human mobility for precision malaria modeling in Zambia
Presentations.organizer: University Consortium for Geographic Information Science (UCGIS)
Presentations.location: University of Maryland, College Park, MD, USA
Presentations.related_project: NSF Award #2451156 (GeoHDR Lab, PI: Dr. Yao Li)
Presentations.abstract: Presents a novel GeoAI deep learning architecture (U-Net deep ensemble) that fuses 38 environmental and infrastructural covariates from Google Earth Engine with annual WorldPop surfaces to downscale aggregate Meta mobility counts (~5.5 km) to a fine 100 m resolution across Zambia under pycnophylactic mass conservation constraints, enabling accurate Human-Vector Contact Zone (HVCZ) malaria risk mapping.

Presentations.title: A spatial perspective on urban land growth: Infrastructure, employment, mobility, and land use change in Tennessee
Presentations.conference: 80th Annual Meeting of the Southeastern Division of the American Association of Geographers (SEDAAG 2025)
Presentations.abstract: Examines how highway capacity projects, spatial employment density clusters, and vehicular mobility jointly drove parcel-level urban growth across Tennessee between 1985 and 2023 using spatial autoregressive econometric modeling.

Presentations.title: Exploring the relationship between road improvements, employment, and land development in Tennessee
Presentations.conference: 2nd Annual Memphis Area Geographic Information Council (MAGIC) Collegiate Geospatial Showcase
Presentations.abstract: First-place award-winning presentation demonstrating spatial modeling workflows to isolate the localized versus regional developmental impacts of road improvements in Tennessee, accounting for accessibility differentials and employment centers.

Presentations.title: Exploring the road improvement impact on induced travel in Tennessee
Presentations.abstract: Investigates facility-level induced travel demand across Tennessee highway corridors using 2SLS instrumental variable regression, highlighting policy implications for state transportation funding and capacity screening criteria.

Presentations.title: Induced travel: An illusion in traffic demand management
Presentations.conference: Institute for Intelligent Systems (IIS) Seminar Series
Presentations.organizer: Institute for Intelligent Systems, The University of Memphis
Presentations.abstract: Critical evaluation of historical traffic demand management paradigms, analyzing whether highway capacity expansions induce demand or merely absorb latent regional mobility needs.
